NDT training in Midland: how it works for Midland employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to Midland and Odessa employers and technicians, as live online classroom sessions plus hands-on practical sessions onsite at your yard, shop or plant. Certification is granted by your employer under its written practice after classroom training, logged field experience, Level III-administered exams and a vision test.

Midland's NDT market is shaped by the pace of the Permian Basin. Operators, midstream companies, pressure-control rental firms, pipe inspection yards and fabrication shops along the I-20 corridor between Midland and Odessa all need certified technicians, and they usually need them fast. Crews rotate between well sites, gathering systems, compressor stations and gas processing plants, and turnover is high. That makes the employer-based SNT-TC-1A model especially important: a technician's certification belongs to the employer's written practice, so each new hire must be brought into that practice with documented training, experience and exams.

Atlantis NDT does not operate a training centre in Midland or anywhere else. Theory is taught live online, which suits technicians who spend long stretches in the field and cannot sit in a classroom for a week, and practical sessions are delivered onsite at the employer's facility on its own equipment, under ASNT Level III oversight. Request a Midland training quote with the methods, levels and head-count you need.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Midland

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge: principles, equipment, calibration, technique, codes and interpretation. Level I prepares technicians to perform calibrations and tests under supervision; Level II covers interpretation and evaluation against codes and specifications, and report writing; Level III preparation covers the basic, method and specific examinations. Recommended training and experience hours come from SNT-TC-1A and are set by your written practice; use the training requirements matrix as your reference.

MethodLevelsWhat Midland employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepWall-thickness surveys on gathering lines, pressure-control iron and production vessels; weld inspection on fabricated skids and station pipingBasic maths; Level II requires Level I training and experience
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepGirth-weld inspection on pipeline construction as an alternative to RT, corrosion mapping on station pipingUT Level II normally required first
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-wall weld inspection on pressure vessels and processing plant equipmentUT Level II normally required first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPipeline girth-weld radiography to API 1104, plant piping to ASME B31.3, film and digital interpretationRadiation safety training plus Texas requirements below
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, II, III prepCrack detection on frac iron, pressure-control equipment, drill-string components, lifting gear and structural weldsNone beyond employer requirements
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, II, III prepStainless and non-ferrous components at gas plants, weld surface inspection on alloy pipingNone beyond employer requirements
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual on pipeline and station construction, thread and connection inspection, general acceptance inspectionNone beyond employer requirements
ET (eddy current testing)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger and air-cooler tube inspection at gas processing plants, surface crack checks on componentsBasic electrical theory helpful

How the methods map to Permian Basin work. The most common entry route for new technicians in Midland is MT and UT, because pressure-control and frac iron recertification, wellhead components, and drill-string inspection lean heavily on magnetic particle and ultrasonic thickness. Pipe inspection yards that serve oil country tubular goods use ultrasonic and electromagnetic inspection, often to API specifications and operator-specific requirements; much of that equipment is specialised, but the underlying UT and electromagnetic principles are the same. Pipeline construction contractors building gathering and transmission lines look for RT and increasingly PAUT for girth welds under API 1104, with VT on every weld. Gas processing plants and compressor stations add ET for exchanger tubing and UT, PT and RT on B31.3 piping.

A practical progression for a Midland newcomer is MT and PT, then UT Level I and II, then either RT or PAUT depending on whether the employer is in construction or integrity work. The full catalogue is on the NDT training page, and experienced technicians can prepare for ASNT Level III.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Midland, step by step

  1. Start with your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice; the employer's written practice turns it into binding rules for that company. It defines levels, training and experience, exams and recertification.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Method theory, equipment, codes and interpretation, delivered live online or in an onsite session. Check the training requirements matrix for recommended hours.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Record hours performing the method under certified supervision. In the Permian, where technicians move between well sites daily, a clean daily log signed by your supervisor saves weeks later.
  4. Pass the general exam. Written questions on method principles, administered under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Written questions on the procedures, equipment and codes your employer uses, such as API 1104 for pipeline welds or ASME B31.3 for plant piping.
  6. Pass the practical exam. Hands-on testing of real specimens with known flaws, graded by the Level III against a documented checklist.
  7. Pass the vision tests. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast differentiation, with near vision repeated annually.
  8. Receive certification from your employer. Issued in writing for each method and level, valid while employed there.
  9. Recertify on schedule. Recertification at the interval in the written practice, with evidence of continued satisfactory performance. A change of employer means recertification under the new written practice.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Midland crews

Live online theory for field-heavy crews. Midland technicians often work long hitches with irregular days off. Live online classroom sessions can be scheduled in blocks that fit around rotations, and technicians can join from home in Midland, Odessa, Big Spring, Andrews or wherever the crew is based. See online NDT training.

Onsite practical at your yard or shop. Hands-on sessions run at the employer's facility using its own flaw detectors, yokes, sources and specimens, under Level III oversight. For a pressure-control company, that means practical training on the actual iron you recertify. For a pipeline contractor, it means weld specimens made to your procedures.

Scheduling around activity levels. Permian activity swings with commodity prices and rig counts. Many employers find the best time to train is during a slower quarter, so that newly certified technicians are ready when work picks up. Gas plant and compressor station operators can schedule training ahead of planned maintenance outages. West Texas summer heat is also a factor for outdoor practical sessions; we plan early starts or indoor shop space where possible. Ask about onsite training for your Midland crew; onsite and cohort quotes are usually returned within one business day.

Corporate programmes. For employers onboarding several technicians at once, a corporate NDT training programme can combine theory, practical sessions, examinations and written-practice support.

Where NDT technicians work in Midland

Upstream production and completions. Operators across the Midland Basin run wells, tank batteries, separators, heater-treaters and flowlines. Completion work uses large volumes of high-pressure flow iron and pressure-control equipment that must be inspected and recertified on a schedule, typically with UT thickness, MT and VT. Employers commonly ask for MT and UT Level II and a clean driving record for field work.

Midstream pipelines and gathering systems. The Permian's gathering, crude, gas and NGL pipelines run in every direction, feeding the Gulf Coast. Construction work is governed by API 1104 for welding and inspection, and transmission and regulated gathering lines fall under federal PHMSA rules in 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, with the Railroad Commission of Texas overseeing intrastate pipeline safety. RT and PAUT for girth welds, and UT for integrity digs, are the core methods.

Gas processing and compressor stations. Cryogenic gas processing plants and compressor stations use piping built to ASME B31.3 and pressure vessels to ASME Section VIII. NDT covers new-construction welds, in-service corrosion monitoring, and exchanger tube inspection with ET.

Pipe inspection yards and OCTG. The Midland-Odessa area has a long-standing cluster of yards inspecting casing, tubing and drill pipe. Work uses ultrasonic and electromagnetic inspection, often following API and operator specifications or industry standards such as DS-1 for drill-stem components. Atlantis does not train to DS-1 or API inspector schemes, but SNT-TC-1A method training underpins the technician's qualification in UT and MT.

Fabrication and machine shops. Skid builders, tank fabricators and machine shops supplying the oilfield weld to AWS D1.1 and ASME codes and need VT, MT and UT capability in house.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program licenses industrial radiography and administers its rules under Title 25 of the Texas Administrative Code, including requirements for radiographer and radiographer trainee qualification and state-recognised certification. Field radiography at temporary job sites requires at least two qualified individuals. These radiation-safety requirements sit alongside SNT-TC-1A method certification, which is still needed to interpret film or digital images. Confirm current requirements directly with DSHS before planning RT work; your employer's radiation safety officer governs that side.

Level III services and written practices for Midland NDT companies

Midland has many small and fast-growing inspection companies, some started by experienced technicians who have gone independent. A common gap is a written practice that has not kept up with the methods the company now performs, or no Level III responsible for exams. Atlantis supports these employers with:

  • Written practice development for new companies, or revision for companies adding methods such as PAUT. See written practice development.
  • Level III examination services: general, specific and practical exams, grading and records.
  • Procedures and technique sheets for UT thickness, MT on pressure-control equipment, API 1104 RT and PAUT, and plant piping inspection.
  • Records audits before an operator or midstream client prequalification audit.
  • Plain-language SNT-TC-1A guidance for owners and managers. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Book a Level III consultation for your Midland or Odessa operation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The oil and gas site and storage tank environments are the closest match to Permian field work, and the welding workshop suits fabrication-shop technicians.

Use it to rehearse set-ups, scan coverage and interpretation decisions between onsite sessions and on rotation days off. It is practice only: it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens, and time in the simulator is not on-the-job experience.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III services, and supervises onsite practical delivery.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Midland

How do I get NDT certified in Midland?

Get hired by, or work for, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete classroom training for the method and level, log supervised field experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision tests. The employer then certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes. Classroom theory is delivered live online anywhere in Texas where the written practice accepts it. Practical training must be hands-on, which Atlantis delivers onsite at your employer's facility. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice and your UT Level I record. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours for each level, listed in our training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer to accumulate than classroom hours.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

The employer must hold a Texas DSHS licence to use radioactive sources, and individual radiographers and trainees must meet Texas qualification and certification requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Confirm current requirements with DSHS.

What does NDT training cost in Midland?

Quote on request. The price depends on method, level, group size, onsite practical requirements and whether exam administration and written-practice work are included. Request a Midland training quote; replies usually arrive within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Midland employers?

Yes, SNT-TC-1A-based certification is the standard framework for industrial NDT in West Texas. Some employers also want AWS CWI for weld inspection roles or API inspector credentials for plant work; Atlantis does not train to those, but the NDT method certification is the foundation.

Which method should I learn first to work in the Permian?

MT and UT are the most requested entry methods for pressure-control, completions and integrity work, with VT on almost every job. RT or PAUT follows for pipeline construction roles.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Midland or Odessa?

No. Theory is taught live online and practical sessions run onsite at the employer's facility.

Can a new Midland inspection company get a written practice from Atlantis?

Yes. We develop SNT-TC-1A written practices, provide Level III exam services and prepare procedures. See written practice development.

How do I prepare for ASNT Level III from West Texas?

Level III preparation runs live online. Practice material such as UT Level 2 practice questions helps refresh fundamentals.

What do NDT technicians earn in the Permian Basin?

Pay swings with activity, method, level and travel. Instead of quoting unreliable local figures, see the NDT salary guide.

Can training be scheduled around rotations?

Yes. Online theory blocks can fit days off, and onsite practical sessions are scheduled with the employer. Ask about a rotation-friendly schedule.
